The authors observe that applying guidance at every timestep can lead to samples that are overly tailored to the guidance model's parameters, rather than generalizing to the desired condition. To mitigate this, Compress Guidance reduces the number of timesteps where guidance is applied, concentrating the guidance steps in the early stages of the sampling process and skipping them in later stages. This approach is motivated by the observation that the guidance loss is primarily active in the early stages of sampling, and becomes less significant as the image structure emerges. The core idea is that by reducing the number of guidance steps, the model is less likely to overfit to the guidance model and more likely to generate images that are faithful to the desired conditions. The method is presented as a way to improve both the quality and diversity of generated images while also reducing the computational cost associated with the sampling process. The authors provide a theoretical justification for their approach, arguing that reducing guidance steps mitigates the model-fitting issue.
